newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 54,000 T of corn - traders.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 54,000 T of corn - traders.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 54,000 tonnes of corn this week following purchases of 162,000 tonnes in the previous week, traders said on Monday.
"Taiwan corn buyers will finish their purchases through September in this week," a Taipei trader said. "One more 54,000-tonne corn shipment will complete all the major buying."
Despite uncertainty over possible further declines in corn prices, Taiwan corn buyers decided to lock in their costs at current prices.
"It's hard to say how far the corn futures (price) can fall, but the current prices are good for profit considerations," one buyer in Taipei said.
Taiwanese soybean buyers have already completed their buying through September, traders said.
Buyers of wheat were expected to stay on the sidelines as most of the island's near-term needs have already been filled.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were quoted at about US$11.00 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico reached $21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized June shipments.
